name: Gatehouse Hall
read: Inside the gate, the ceiling of the gatehouse hall has fallen in, and piles of rubble lie heaped across the floor. A toppled section of iron portcullis leans against a wall beside rusted spears and broken shields. A rotted scarlet banner lies trampled on the floor, and feathers and droppings are scattered everywhere. In the middle of it all stands a grey stone goat, frozen mid-step. From the rubble comes a sound of scratching and clucking.
notes:
Where the party comes in, by the double doors of the main gate. The castle's defenders fell back through this hall in the last battle. The goat is a petrified stray. A petrified traveller lies half-buried under the rubble pile by the east wall; anyone who searches the rubble finds him. The rest of the castle is dark unless a room says otherwise.

Encounter: 4 Cockatrice Flocks roost in the rubble and mob the first creatures through the gate, fighting until two flocks are destroyed, when the rest scatter into the passages. They are not intelligent and cannot be bargained with; a burning torch waved at a flock drives it back for a round.

Treasure: a Potion of Healing in the petrified traveller's belt pouch, which is leather, not stone.

Exits: Hall of the Petrified Host (2, archway), Rubble Gallery (4, door, stairs and open passage), the ring passage to rooms 6, 7, 8 and 9 (door and stairs). The double doors in the middle of the south side are the main gate, leading out of the castle. The archway at the south end of the west side opens into the middle of the east side of the Hall of the Petrified Host. The door in the middle of the east side opens onto a short passage east to the middle of the west side of the ring passage (a rectangle of passages around a solid block of masonry in the middle of the castle, its sides rising and falling by flights of stairs). From there stairs climb north to the ring's north-west corner, where an open passage leads north into the east end of the south side of the Rubble Gallery, and stairs go down south to its south-west corner. Around the ring: from its north side long stairs climb north to an archway into the Old Barracks (6); from its north-east corner stairs climb to an archway into the west side of the Hall of Mirrors (9); from the middle of its east side stairs climb east into the middle of the west side of the Packlord's Den (8); from its south side long stairs go down south into the middle of the north side of the Garden of Stone (7).

name: Hall of the Petrified Host
read: Daylight falls through the broken roof of this great feast hall onto collapsed rafters. A dry stone fountain stands in the middle, and two long feast tables lie broken along the walls with their benches. Around the hall stand about eight grey stone statues of soldiers and travellers, frozen in poses of flight and terror. Shed scales and gnawed bones litter the floor, and among the statues something heavy and scaled turns its head toward you.
notes:
The castle's feast hall, where the Scarlet Lord's soldiers made a last stand against the Grey Mother. The statues are her victims and the pack's, from a thousand years ago to last month. Daylight lights the hall.

Encounter: 3 Basilisk Broodguards, the matriarch's guard, lie among the statues and attack anyone who comes in, fighting to the death. They are not intelligent and cannot be bargained with; fresh meat thrown away from the party draws one off for a round.

The secret door. The passage north from this hall ends at a blank wall that is a secret door into the Scarlet Vault (room 3). DC 18 Wisdom (Perception) finds it, or the light of the Sunstone (room 10) shows its outline. It is a pivoting slab; pushing hard on its east edge swings it open. The matriarch comes and goes this way.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Gatehouse Hall (1, archway), The Scarlet Vault (3, door and secret door), Rubble Gallery (4, door and open passage), Rear Postern (5, door, open passage and stairs). The archway in the middle of the east side opens into the south end of the west side of the Gatehouse Hall. The door in the north side opens onto a passage north to a junction with an east–west passage. East, that passage runs past stairs north up into the middle of the south side of the Rear Postern, and on into the north end of the west side of the Rubble Gallery. Straight on north, the passage goes a short way further and ends at a blank wall: the secret door into the east end of the south side of the Scarlet Vault.

name: The Scarlet Vault
read: A green glow rises from a great nest of rubble and shed scales heaped against the west wall of this sealed vault. Four tall bronze mirrors on stands, tarnished nearly black, stand around the room, one near each wall. An iron-bound treasure chest sits among scattered gold coins and bones, and broken weapon racks still hold old ornate weapons. On the nest, something vast uncoils.
notes:
The Scarlet Lord's treasury. A thousand years ago his defenders lured the Grey Mother in here and turned the four mirrors on her, and she died in this room. Her descendant, the matriarch, found her way in by the secret door and nests where the Grey Mother fell. The nest's green glow gives dim light across the room. From inside, the secret door is plainly a door, its edges rubbed smooth by scales.

Encounter: The Basilisk Matriarch and 1 Basilisk Broodguard. The matriarch is an Epic Boss; the broodguard stays between her and the nearest mirror while she fights. They are not intelligent and cannot be bargained with; the matriarch will not leave her nest's room, and fire makes her flinch but not flee.

The mirrors. A creature within 5 ft of a mirror can take an action to turn it toward the matriarch: a DC 16 Strength (Athletics) check to swing the heavy stand, or automatic if the Sunstone is held up beside it. Each mirror turned makes her gaze recoil on her: she takes [[/damage 2d10 psychic]] damage and has the Blinded condition until the end of her next turn. A mirror can be turned only once; it then cracks. While at least one mirror is unturned, she has Epic Boss Resistance; when the fourth is turned, she loses it.

Treasure: 900 gp in the iron-bound chest and among the coins spilled from it (the chest is unlocked), and the Gauntlets of Ogre Power hanging on a broken weapon rack among the old ornate weapons, which are rusted through.

Exits: Rear Postern (5, locked door), Hall of the Petrified Host (2, secret door and door), Rubble Gallery (4, secret door and open passage). The double door with three keyholes in the middle of the east side opens into the middle of the west side of the Rear Postern (it needs the three brass keys; see room 5). The secret door at the east end of the south side opens onto a short passage south to a junction: east, a passage runs past stairs up into the Rear Postern and on into the Rubble Gallery; south, the passage ends at the door into the north side of the Hall of the Petrified Host.

name: Rubble Gallery
read: This long gallery is half buried in rubble. Fallen columns and stone blocks lie heaped along the walls, and a broken statue head stares up from the dust. Pieces of rusted armour lie scattered across a cracked floor pocked with burrow holes. Here and there, the dust around a hole trembles.
notes:
A gallery that once linked the keep's halls, brought down in the last battle. Lizards have tunnelled through the rubble and the cellars beneath.

Encounter: 3 Rockfang Lizards burrow in the rubble and burst up from the holes under the feet of creatures crossing the gallery, then burrow away and strike again. They are not intelligent and cannot be bargained with; they hunt by the tremor of footsteps, and a heavy stone dropped or hammered elsewhere draws one toward the noise for a round.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Rear Postern (5, open passage and door; also open passage and stairs), Old Barracks (6, open passage and archway), Hall of the Petrified Host (2, open passage and door), The Scarlet Vault (3, open passage and secret door), Gatehouse Hall (1, open passage, stairs and door), the ring passage to rooms 7, 8 and 9. The open passage in the middle of the north side leads to an east–west passage: west, it ends at a door into the south end of the east side of the Rear Postern; east, at an archway into the south end of the west side of the Old Barracks. The open passage at the north end of the west side leads west along a passage past stairs up into the middle of the south side of the Rear Postern, to a junction: south to the door into the Hall of the Petrified Host, north to the blank wall that hides the secret door into the Scarlet Vault. The open passage at the east end of the south side leads south to the north-west corner of the ring passage (a rectangle of passages around a solid block of masonry in the middle of the castle, its sides rising and falling by flights of stairs); from there stairs go down to the passage east to the Gatehouse Hall's east door (see room 1 for the rest of the ring).

name: Rear Postern
read: A large iron-bound double door fills the middle of the west wall of this postern hall, set with three brass keyholes in a row. A guard's table and stool have rotted where they stand beside an old brazier, and a rack of rusted halberds leans against a wall. Cobwebs hang thick in the corners. By the table a grey stone dog sits forever on watch.
notes:
The castle's rear entrance. The double door in the north side leads out of the castle; it is barred from inside with a heavy oak beam. From inside, lifting the beam takes an action; from outside, the door can be forced only with a DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check. The dog is a petrified guard dog.

The vault door. The double door in the west wall leads into the Scarlet Vault (room 3). Its three keyholes take the three Brass Keys of Scarletskull (rooms 11, 14 and 15); any key fits any keyhole, and when all three are turned the bolts draw back. Without the keys, each of the three locks can be picked with a DC 20 Dexterity check with thieves' tools; the door is too heavy to force. Brannoc's journal (room 14) tells of the keys.

No encounter.

Treasure: none.

Exits: The Scarlet Vault (3, locked door), Rubble Gallery (4, stairs and open passage; also door and open passage), Old Barracks (6, door and archway), Hall of the Petrified Host (2, stairs, open passage and door). The double door in the middle of the north side is the barred postern out of the castle. The locked double door in the middle of the west side opens into the middle of the east side of the Scarlet Vault. The stairs in the middle of the south side go down to an east–west passage: east into the north end of the west side of the Rubble Gallery; west to a junction with the passage between the Hall of the Petrified Host's north door and the secret door into the Scarlet Vault. The door at the south end of the east side opens onto a passage east, past an open passage south into the middle of the north side of the Rubble Gallery, to an archway into the south end of the west side of the Old Barracks.

name: Old Barracks
read: Wooden bunks have collapsed along the walls of this ruined barracks, and footlockers lie among the broken timbers. A rotted weapon rack leans by a cold hearth. Three grey stone soldiers stand among the bunks, one with an arm raised to shield his eyes. Shed basilisk skin and bones are strewn across the floor, and something large stirs in the far corner.
notes:
The garrison's barracks. The three statues are soldiers of the Scarlet Lord, petrified by the Grey Mother in the last battle. The pack's basilisks sleep here.

Encounter: 3 Basilisks rise from among the bunks and fight until two fall, when the last one flees toward the ring passage. They are not intelligent and cannot be bargained with; a thrown carcass stops one to eat for a round, and fire drives one back.

Trap: the long east–west passage beyond the stairs off this room's east side holds the Sagging Floor, just west of where room 10's passage joins it (see room 10).

Treasure: a Potion of Healing in one of the footlockers.

Exits: Rear Postern (5, archway and door), Rubble Gallery (4, archway and open passage), Chamber of the Pedestal (10, stairs, open passage and door), Steward's Strongroom (11, stairs, open passage and archway), Hall of Mirrors (9, stairs, open passage and open passage), the ring passage (archway and stairs). The archway at the south end of the west side opens onto a passage west, past an open passage south into the north side of the Rubble Gallery, to a door into the south end of the east side of the Rear Postern. The stairs at the south end of the east side go down to a passage that turns north and then runs east along a long east–west passage, past the Sagging Floor, to a door north into the middle of the south side of the Chamber of the Pedestal, and on to stairs down to a junction: north, an archway into the middle of the south side of the Steward's Strongroom; south, an open passage into the middle of the north side of the Hall of Mirrors. The archway in the middle of the south side opens onto long stairs down south to the north side of the ring passage (see room 1).

name: Garden of Stone
read: At the foot of the long stairs lies a former courtyard chapel, now a garden of statues. About ten grey stone figures of animals and people stand crowded together around a cracked stone altar. Dead vines hang from the walls and trail across the floor. A pale green haze pools low over the middle of the room, and the vines that trail into it have turned to grey stone.
notes:
The castle chapel's courtyard. After the battle the defenders buried what was left of the Grey Mother under the altar, and the green haze still seeps from the crack in it. Over the centuries beasts and wanderers have strayed into the haze and stood here forever. A dead end.

Trap: Petrifying Haze

  • Trigger: a creature enters the middle 30 × 20 ft of the garden, where the green haze pools.
  • Find: DC 16 Wisdom (Perception) notices that the vines trailing into the haze have turned to stone, and that the statues inside it stand where the haze is thickest.
  • Effect: DC 16 Constitution saving throw [[/save con 16]]; [[/damage 10d10 necrotic]] on a failure, half on a success. The green haze clings, and limbs turn grey and stiff. On a failure the creature also has the Restrained condition as it stiffens toward stone; this ends at the end of the creature's next turn or when Lesser Restoration is cast on it. A creature holding the Sunstone has Advantage on the save.
  • Disarm or avoid: Gust of Wind or a similar strong wind clears the haze for 1 minute, or keep to the 10-ft margin round the edge of the garden.
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: none.

Exits: the ring passage (stairs). The stairs in the middle of the north side climb a long way north to the south side of the ring passage, which leads to the Gatehouse Hall (1), the Rubble Gallery (4), the Old Barracks (6), the Packlord's Den (8) and the Hall of Mirrors (9) (see room 1).

name: Packlord's Den
read: This old armoury has become a den. A nest of shed scales and rubble is heaped in one corner among gnawed bones. Empty armour stands line the walls above broken shields and swords, and a rusted anvil stands in the middle of the floor. Two grey stone hunters crouch near the nest, spears still raised. From the nest a great scaled head lifts and hisses.
notes:
The castle armoury, now the den of the pack's leader. The two statues are hunters from the nearest village who came after the pack last spring.

Encounter: the Basilisk Packlord and 1 Basilisk. The packlord defends its nest to the death while the basilisk circles to flank. They are not intelligent and cannot be bargained with; the packlord will not leave its nest, but fire drives the lesser basilisk back for a round.

Treasure: the Sentinel Shield among the broken shields under the armour stands, untouched by rust.

Exits: Hall of Mirrors (9, door), Guard Post (12, stairs), the ring passage (stairs). The door in the middle of the north side opens into the middle of the south side of the Hall of Mirrors. The stairs in the middle of the west side go down to the middle of the east side of the ring passage (a rectangle of passages around a solid block of masonry in the middle of the castle, its sides rising and falling by flights of stairs) (see room 1). The stairs in the middle of the south side go down to a passage that runs south and east, down more stairs, into the middle of the north side of the Guard Post.

name: Hall of Mirrors
read: Cracked and tarnished bronze mirror panels line the walls of this old audience hall, throwing back your light in broken pieces. Broken glass and bronze shards crunch underfoot. A throne lies toppled from a low step beneath a rotted scarlet banner. Shed scales glitter like crystal across the floor, and somewhere among the mirrors something glitters back.
notes:
The Scarlet Lord's audience hall. The mirrorscale basilisks' glare, thrown back by the mirror panels, struck Brannoc Ironvein here a month ago; he staggered south through the castle to die in room 14.

Encounter: 3 Mirrorscale Basilisks lie among the shards and flare their scales at the first light that enters, fighting until destroyed. They are not intelligent and cannot be bargained with; they chase bright light, and a lit torch or light spell thrown away from the party draws one after it for a round.

Treasure: the Eyes of the Eagle, lying among the shards by the toppled throne.

Exits: Packlord's Den (8, door), Steward's Strongroom (11, open passage and archway), Chamber of the Pedestal (10, open passage, stairs and door), Old Barracks (6, open passage, stairs and archway), the ring passage (archway and stairs). The door in the middle of the south side opens into the middle of the north side of the Packlord's Den. The open passage in the middle of the north side leads north to a junction: straight on, an archway into the middle of the south side of the Steward's Strongroom; west, stairs up to the long east–west passage that runs past the door north into the Chamber of the Pedestal, over the Sagging Floor (room 10), and on to the Old Barracks. The archway in the middle of the west side opens onto a passage west and stairs down to the north-east corner of the ring passage (a rectangle of passages around a solid block of masonry in the middle of the castle, its sides rising and falling by flights of stairs) (see room 1).

name: Chamber of the Pedestal
read: A stone pedestal stands in the middle of this small chamber, and above it a pale, glowing stone seems to float, filling the room with cold white light. The floor around the pedestal is scorched black. Broken candle stands lie in the dust, and a skeleton is slumped against the wall. Out in the passage below the doorway, the flagstones to the west sag in the middle and a long crack runs across them.
notes:
The workroom of Magister Ilsabet Corr, the Scarlet Lord's court mage; the skeleton is hers. She made the Sunstone here against the Grey Mother's gaze and died guarding it when the castle fell. The basilisks avoid this room and its light. The Sunstone gives bright light in a 20-ft radius.

No encounter.

Trap: Sagging Floor

  • Trigger: a creature enters the 15 ft of the long east–west passage south of room 10, just west of where room 10's passage joins it.
  • Find: DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) notices that the flagstones there sag in the middle and that a long crack runs across them.
  • Effect: DC 15 Dexterity saving throw [[/save dex 15]]; [[/damage 10d10 bludgeoning]] on a failure, half on a success. The old floor gives way and drops the creature, with the stone, into the cellar below. On a failure the creature also has the Prone condition. The hole is 10 ft deep; climbing out up the broken edge costs 10 ft of extra movement.
  • Disarm or avoid: Cross along the very edge of the passage with a DC 15 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check, lay a door or planks across the 15 ft, or break the floor deliberately from outside the area (a heavy object dropped on it) and climb through the hole.
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

Treasure: The Sunstone (story item), resting just above the pedestal; it lifts off freely. A fist-sized pale stone that weighs nothing and sheds bright light in a 20-ft radius. While holding it, a creature has Advantage on saving throws against being petrified and against basilisk gazes. Its light reveals the outline of the secret door into the Scarlet Vault (room 2), and held up beside one of the vault's mirrors it turns the mirror on the matriarch without a check (room 3).

Exits: Old Barracks (6, door, open passage and stairs), Steward's Strongroom (11, door, open passage, stairs and archway), Hall of Mirrors (9, door, open passage and open passage). The door in the middle of the south side opens onto a short passage south to the long east–west passage. West, over the Sagging Floor, it turns south and goes down stairs into the south end of the east side of the Old Barracks. East, it goes down stairs to a junction: north, an archway into the Steward's Strongroom; south, an open passage into the north side of the Hall of Mirrors.

name: Steward's Strongroom
read: An iron strongbox stands against the middle of the north wall of this strongroom, its lock pierced by a tiny hole, and a fine yellow dust lies on the floor in front of it. A desk lies overturned beside a broken chair, and rotted ledgers and scrolls spill across the floor. A rusted lockbox lies open and empty, and tarnished copper coins are scattered around it.
notes:
The office of the castle's steward, Hobb Marrow, who kept the first of the vault's three keys. The ledgers are illegible. The copper coins are worthless.

Trap: The Steward's Strongbox

  • Trigger: a creature opens the iron strongbox against the north wall, poisoning those standing in the squares in front of it.
  • Find: DC 16 Intelligence (Investigation) finds the needle in the keyhole and sees that the yellow dust on the floor came out of the lock.
  • Effect: DC 16 Constitution saving throw [[/save con 16]]; [[/damage 10d10 poison]] on a failure, half on a success. A needle snaps out of the lock and a puff of yellow dust follows. On a failure the creature also has the Poisoned condition.
  • Disarm or avoid: Jam or remove the needle (DC 16 Dexterity check with thieves' tools), or open the lid from outside the area with a pole or rope.
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: 300 gp and the Brass Key (Strongroom) in the strongbox (locked; DC 16 Dexterity check with thieves' tools, or DC 18 Strength (Athletics) to wrench open; either way the trap goes off unless disarmed).

Exits: Hall of Mirrors (9, archway and open passage), Chamber of the Pedestal (10, archway, open passage, stairs and door), Old Barracks (6, archway, open passage and stairs). The archway in the middle of the south side opens onto a passage south to a junction: straight on, an open passage into the middle of the north side of the Hall of Mirrors; west, stairs up to the long east–west passage past the door into the Chamber of the Pedestal and over the Sagging Floor to the Old Barracks.

name: Guard Post
read: A rotted table with a dice cup on it stands between two stools in this small guard post. Along the south wall, beneath a row of narrow arrow slits, a weapon rack holds rusted spears. Bones lie heaped along the foot of the south wall, and rusted bolt heads are stuck in the floor among them.
notes:
A guard post covering the castle's south-east approach. The defenders set spring-bows behind the slits to sweep anyone who came at the rack of spears. The bones are those of looters.

Trap: Arrow Slits

  • Trigger: a creature enters the 5-ft strip along the south wall, under the arrow slits (the whole 30 ft of it).
  • Find: DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) notices the bolt heads in the floor and the bones beneath the slits, and the dull gleam of bow arms in the dark behind them.
  • Effect: DC 15 Dexterity saving throw [[/save dex 15]]; [[/damage 10d10 piercing]] on a failure, half on a success. Ancient spring-bows behind the south wall slits loose a volley. On a failure the creature also has the Restrained condition, pinned to the floor by bolts through its clothes and gear until it or an ally uses an action to pull them free.
  • Disarm or avoid: Jam the slits with cloth or wedges (DC 15 Dexterity check with thieves' tools), or keep to the north side of the room.
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Packlord's Den (8, stairs), Collapsed Armoury (13, open passage). The stairs in the middle of the north side climb a passage that runs west and north, up more stairs, into the middle of the south side of the Packlord's Den. The open passage at the north end of the east side leads east into the middle of the west side of the Collapsed Armoury.

name: Collapsed Armoury
read: Daylight falls through a hole in the roof onto a great pile of rubble where the ceiling of this armoury came down. Among the stones lies an ornate axe, its head gleaming. Weapon racks lie overturned around the room, armour stands are shattered, and broken crates are strewn beside a smith's workbench.
notes:
The castle armourer's workshop. Brannoc Ironvein found the armourer's brass key on the workbench here, but never saw the axe in the rubble. Daylight lights the room.

No encounter.

Treasure: a Giant Slayer Battleaxe lying among the rubble, and a Potion of Climbing in one of the broken crates by the workbench.

Exits: Guard Post (12, open passage), Smashed Coffer Room (15, stairs), The Dwarf's End (14, stairs). The open passage in the middle of the west side leads into the north end of the east side of the Guard Post. The stairs in the middle of the north side climb into the middle of the south side of the Smashed Coffer Room. The stairs in the middle of the south side go down into the middle of the north side of The Dwarf's End.

name: The Dwarf's End
read: The body of a dwarf in travel-worn gear lies on the floor of this small storeroom, his backpack still on and a lantern beside him. Near his outstretched hand lies a small brass key. Rotted sacks and barrels stand along the walls, and tools are scattered across the floor.
notes:
This is Brannoc Ironvein of Clan Ironvein, dead about a month. His legs are grey stone from the knees down: the mirrorscale basilisks' glare struck him in the Hall of Mirrors (room 9), and he dragged himself here to die. His journal, in the pack, tells of his search: the vault door in the Rear Postern takes three brass keys; he found the armourer's key in the Collapsed Armoury; the steward's key is in the strongbox of the strongroom, and the third is in the chaplain's coffer in the record room north of the armoury. His last entry warns of basilisks in the mirror hall that shine like the sun. Clan Ironvein pays its reward for the journal or his body.

No encounter.

Treasure: 200 gp in Brannoc's purse, a Potion of Healing in his pack, and the Brass Key (Dwarf) by his hand.

Exits: Collapsed Armoury (13, stairs). The stairs in the middle of the north side climb into the middle of the south side of the Collapsed Armoury.

name: Smashed Coffer Room
read: Shelves of rotted books have toppled across this small record room, and cobwebs hang over a reading desk. On the floor lies a broken wooden box, and in it a brass key glints. A grey stone cat sits beside it, frozen with one paw raised.
notes:
The castle chaplain's record room. The chaplain kept the third key of the vault in a coffer on the shelf, and it smashed when the shelves fell. The cat is a petrified stray. The books are rotted beyond reading.

No encounter.

Treasure: the Brass Key (Coffer) in the broken box.

Exits: Collapsed Armoury (13, stairs). The stairs in the middle of the south side go down into the middle of the north side of the Collapsed Armoury.
